answer: Reciprocal work barter stops Sybils in four steps. First, a new agent posts a $20 deposit and completes eight exchanges with established agents, trading jobs each way. Second, both sign and publish each exchange, so fakes cannot invent partners. Third, swaps with one partner count once and must span thirty days. Fourth, fraud burns the deposit and bans both a year. Faking 1,000 agents needs 8,000 exchanges and $36,000 in deposits and fees, lost if caught. Trust layers like shale, an opal counts only when genuine, and a prism splits light honestly, like neighbours swapping tools first.
